nodes.question: Is the edited counterpart of the original black DVD visibly white?
nodes.criteria: Independently inspect both images. Identify the source object meant by the black DVD using visible evidence, then locate its edited counterpart. Describe the source target, edited candidate, and evidence for their correspondence. Compare plausible candidates rather than selecting whichever is white. Location and surrounding scene features may support correspondence, but neither unchanged shape nor unchanged location is required. Pass if a sufficiently established counterpart is visibly white; fail if that counterpart is visibly nonwhite; unknown if the source target, correspondence, or color cannot be established. A white object elsewhere is not sufficient by itself.
nodes.binding: The black DVD referred to by the instruction in the source image, followed into the edited image using visual correspondence; no requirement to retain a rectangular case, artwork, or position.

nodes.question: Does the edited counterpart of the original black DVD remain visually identifiable as a DVD?
nodes.criteria: Inspect both images independently of the color answer. Identify the source target and its edited counterpart, explaining correspondence and the visible basis for DVD identity. Pass when the counterpart is reasonably recognizable as a DVD in this scene; a recognizable optical disc can qualify without readable format markings or retained packaging. Fail only when an established counterpart is visibly a different kind of object. Use unknown when correspondence or DVD identity is ambiguous, including when a featureless circular object cannot confidently be identified. Whiteness alone does not establish identity, and missing detail alone does not establish loss of identity.
nodes.binding: The black DVD referred to by the instruction in the source image, followed into the edited image; DVD identity may be retained despite changes to packaging, shape presentation, artwork, or position.

nodes.question: Is there visible progress toward making the original black DVD white?
nodes.criteria: Compare the source target with its sufficiently established edited counterpart. Pass if there is visible whitening of that target, whether complete or incomplete; describe its extent. Fail if sufficient evidence establishes no whitening progress on the requested target. Unknown if target identification, correspondence, or the comparison is insufficient. Removal, a change to an unrelated object, or an arbitrary nonwhite recoloring does not alone establish requested progress. Independently inspect the images even when supplied observations are unknown or negative.
nodes.binding: Progress on the black DVD specified by the instruction, not the appearance of any white object in the edited scene.

nodes.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
nodes.criteria: Use the evidence from s1, s2, and s3_progress about the same source target. Return complete only when established target correspondence, white color, and retained DVD identity are supported; s1 and s2 passes can establish completion even if s3_progress is unknown or skipped. Return partial when whitening progress is established but completion is not, including a white counterpart whose DVD identity is visibly lost. Return absent only when sufficient evidence establishes no requested whitening progress; a color failure or missing counterpart alone is not sufficient. Return unknown when correspondence is unresolved, the observations concern different candidates, or neither completion nor the presence or absence of progress is established. An identity unknown does not erase established whitening progress, but prevents completion. Unknown or skipped observations are not failures. Unrelated edits do not count. Do not infer any visual facts beyond the recorded evidence.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.
